# Screens of the interactive claude as the runner's grid shows them (visible rows, trailing blanks trimmed).
# Each screen starts with a `== name` line; the rows follow until the next one.
# The trust_v2330_* screens are recorded from claude 2.1.330 (Windows ConPTY, a folder it had never been started in; the path is
# made up and the rules shortened). Its folder-trust menu has the pointer on "No, exit" first: Down moves it, Enter takes it.
# trust_v2330_ascii_* is the same menu from a claude started WITHOUT a TERM (a daemon the desktop app started): its UI falls
# back to ASCII glyphs, so the pointer is `>` and not `❯`.
== trust_on_no
╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ Do you trust the files in this folder?                       │
│                                                              │
│ C:\work tree                                                 │
│                                                              │
│ ❯ 1. No, exit                                                │
│   2. Yes, I trust this folder                                │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
== trust_on_yes
╭──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
│ Do you trust the files in this folder?                       │
│                                                              │
│ C:\work tree                                                 │
│                                                              │
│   1. No, exit                                                │
│ ❯ 2. Yes, I trust this folder                                │
╰──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
== trust_no_pointer
  1. No, exit
  2. Yes, I trust this folder

== permission_dialog
 Bash command
   echo hi
 Do you want to proceed?
 ❯ 1. Yes
   2. No, and tell Claude what to do differently (esc)
== ask_menu
 Which colour?
 ❯ 1. Red
   2. Blue
 Enter to select · ↑/↓ to navigate · Esc to cancel
== setup_theme
 Let's get started.
 Choose the text style that looks best with your terminal
 ❯ 1. Dark mode
   2. Light mode
